label: Ubiquiti airMAX LiteBeam M5 23dBi
description: airMAX 5 GHz CPE/base station with a 23 dBi integrated dish and one 10/100 Ethernet port with passive PoE in. Sold as a 2-pack in this SKU.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking Interface **(1) 10/100 MbE RJ45 port**, Power Method **Passive PoE 2-pair (4, 5+; 7, 8 return)**, 24V 0.2A adapter included, max power consumption 7 W, operating range -40 to 70 C. Two things matter for a plan: the port is **fast Ethernet, so 100 Mbps is a hard ceiling on any airMAX link** built on this radio regardless of what the radio negotiates, and the PoE is **passive 24 V**, not 802.3af, so a standard PoE switch port will not power it. The SKU in the request is a 2-pack (LBE-M5-23-KIT): two units, one model entry.

label: Ubiquiti airMAX Rocket 2AC Prism
description: airMAX ac base station: one gigabit RJ45 port with passive PoE, 2x2 5 GHz radio and RP-SMA connectors for external antennas.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking Interface **(1) GbE RJ45 port**, Power Method passive PoE 2-pair, 24V 0.5A gigabit adapter included, max power consumption 9.5 W, RF connectors **(2) RP-SMA (waterproof) plus (1) GPS**. **No antenna is included** - an RP-SMA Rocket is only as good as the dish or sector you bolt to it, so the radio figure here is the interface's capability, not a link budget.

label: Ubiquiti AmpliFi Alien (router + MeshPoint)
description: Wi-Fi 6 mesh kit: router with 1x GbE WAN and 4x GbE LAN, MeshPoint with 1x GbE LAN, 2.4/5 GHz radios with a touchscreen.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: **Router: (1) GbE RJ45 WAN and (4) GbE RJ45 LAN; MeshPoint: (1) GbE RJ45 LAN**, universal AC input, max power consumption 35 W (router) and 34 W (MeshPoint). The kit is modelled as one device carrying the router's port set: **the MeshPoint adds a second unit with a single LAN port**, so a two-node mesh in a plan needs two entries or a note, not one box with nine ports. The per-band radio rates were not in the extracted rows, so the two radios carry AX3000-class figures and should be read as class rather than a quoted row.

label: Ubiquiti airMAX CRM Point
description: airMAX network management appliance: one 10/100 management port plus two 27V DC Power TransPort outputs for powering airMAX radios.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking interface **(1) 10/100 MbE RJ45 LAN port**, management interface Ethernet in-band plus Bluetooth, Power TransPort output **27V DC at 100 W with one adapter, 200 W with two**, supplied by two 27V 4.4A adapters. This is a **management and power appliance, not a router or a switch**: it has one 100M port and controls radios over the air, so a lab that wires it into a data path will see a 100 Mbps bottleneck and no forwarding at all.
